# ABB: Secure Cloud Network – Traffic Control Domains (Consolidated)

**← Back to [EAP Home](../../../../README.md) • [Strategy](../../../README.md) • [Guidance](../../README.md) • [Network](./README.md)**

> **TOGAF Artifact Type:** Architecture Building Block (ABB) — Child of [GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-ABB](./GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-ABB-v1.md)
>
> This document defines the **consolidated traffic control domain model** for the Platform Gainwell Secure Cloud Network. It specifies the architectural composition of each traffic control domain's boundary — not the AWS services, configurations, or operational procedures used to realize it. The corresponding Solution Building Blocks (SBBs) realize this ABB for specific technology contexts.

[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#1-motivation]

## 1. Motivation

**ADR-SEC-PG-001** established that all Platform Gainwell traffic must be classified into one of four explicitly governed domains: External-In, Internal-Out, East-West, and Intra-VPC. The parent Secure Cloud Network ABB (`GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-ABB`) defined the network's structural elements — account topology, VPC organization, the taxonomy of the four domains, and the high-level required properties each domain boundary must satisfy.

What neither document addresses is the **internal architecture of a domain control boundary** — the structural components that must be present at every boundary, how a boundary decides to permit or deny a flow, what it must emit, and what it must do when it cannot make a decision. Without this definition:

- Downstream SBBs have no canonical behavioral contract to realize
- Security standards authors lack an architectural specification to impose requirements against
- Security operations teams lack a defined set of observable signals that domain boundaries must produce
- Platform engineers cannot consistently determine whether a proposed implementation satisfies or violates the domain model

This ABB addresses that gap. It defines the **Control Boundary Pattern (CBP)** — a reusable architectural pattern that all four traffic domains instantiate — and then specifies how each domain instantiates it: what entry and exit conditions apply, what a valid policy assertion looks like, how control authority is structured within the domain, and what happens when control is unavailable.

---

### In Scope

This ABB governs:

- The Control Boundary Pattern (CBP) as a reusable architectural element all four traffic domains instantiate
- Per-domain architectural specification: entry conditions, control authority model, exit conditions, policy assertion requirements, and fail-closed behavior
- The domain handoff model — the architectural contract governing what passes between domains when traffic transitions
- The observability model — what minimum observable signals each domain control boundary must produce
- The interfaces this ABB provides to downstream domain-specific SBBs and child ABBs
- The constraints that no SBB or implementation may violate
page_texts.8:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#out-of-scope]

### Out of Scope

This ABB **does not** define:

- **Specific AWS services** used to realize any domain's control boundary — those are SBB concerns
- **Security standards or control thresholds** — enforcement parameters, acceptance criteria, and SLA requirements are standards artifacts
- **Network topology or account structure** — covered by the parent ABB (`GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-ABB`)
- **Implementation configurations** — security group rules, routing policies, or tool configurations
- **Operational procedures** — monitoring runbooks, incident response procedures, and change management processes
- **Per-domain audit log formats or schemas** — format is a standards concern; this ABB defines what must be auditable, not how it is recorded

[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#51-pattern-definition]

### 5.1 Pattern Definition

The **Control Boundary Pattern (CBP)** is the canonical architectural pattern from which all four Platform Gainwell traffic control domains are derived. It describes the required structural composition of any boundary at which a platform traffic domain boundary is enforced.

The CBP exists because NIST SP 800-207 and ADR-SEC-PG-001 both require that **every traffic domain boundary enforce an explicit policy decision before traffic traverses it**. That requirement implies a consistent structural pattern — not uniform technology, but a consistent set of components whose presence can be architecturally verified and against which standards can impose enforceable requirements.

A domain boundary that does not exhibit the CBP structure is architecturally non-conformant regardless of the technology used.
page_texts.12:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#52-cbp-structural-components]

### 5.2 CBP Structural Components

Every instantiation of the Control Boundary Pattern must exhibit the following four structural components. Each component is defined by what it must structurally do, not by what technology realizes it:

---
page_texts.13:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#component-1-decision-engine]

#### Component 1: Decision Engine

**What it does:** Evaluates each traffic flow against applicable policy to produce an explicit binary outcome — permit or deny — before that flow is allowed to proceed.

**Required properties:**

- Each evaluation is **per-flow** or **per-request**, not aggregate or session-wide with blanket trust extended after initial evaluation
- Evaluation inputs must include at minimum: **claimed identity** of the traffic initiator, **target resource or service**, and **policy context** applicable to the requested access
- The outcome must be **deterministic for a given set of inputs and policy state** — non-deterministic behavior (e.g., random permit) is not an acceptable fail-open substitute
- Absence of an applicable policy results in a **deny** outcome; no default permit exists
page_texts.14:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#component-2-enforcement-point]

#### Component 2: Enforcement Point

**What it does:** Acts on the Decision Engine's outcome by permitting the traffic flow to proceed or terminating it.

**Required properties:**

- The Enforcement Point is **logically and functionally distinct from the workload** it protects; a workload cannot serve as its own Enforcement Point
- Enforcement is **synchronous with the traffic flow** — the flow does not reach its destination until enforcement has acted on the Decision Engine's outcome
- The Enforcement Point can **terminate TLS and re-originate** where necessary for inspection, but must not permanently decrypt PHI/PII in a manner inconsistent with transmission security requirements
- The Enforcement Point is **positioned by the architecture**, not by workload preference; a workload cannot opt-out of traversing the Enforcement Point for its domain
page_texts.15:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#component-3-audit-emitter]

#### Component 3: Audit Emitter

**What it does:** Generates an audit-quality record for every policy decision — permit and deny — at the time of the decision.

**Required properties:**

- Audit records are emitted **at decision time**, not deferred or batched in a way that could produce gaps if the system crashes after permitting a flow
- Each record must be sufficient to reconstruct: who or what initiated the flow, what resource was targeted, what policy was evaluated, and what outcome was reached
- Audit records are **tamper-evident** — they are written to an output that the decision-making process itself cannot retroactively modify
- The Audit Emitter's output path is **architecturally separate from the workload** it monitors; the workload's operational state does not gate the production or delivery of audit records
- The Audit Emitter is a required structural component of any CBP instantiation; a domain boundary without audit output realizes a different pattern
page_texts.16:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#component-4-exception-handler]

#### Component 4: Exception Handler

**What it does:** Defines and enforces the boundary's behavior when the Decision Engine is unavailable, incapacitated, or unable to produce an outcome within an acceptable time bound.

**Required properties:**

- The Exception Handler **defaults to deny** in all cases where the Decision Engine cannot produce a permit outcome; this is the fail-closed requirement
- The Exception Handler must **generate an audit record** indicating that the exception occurred, including timestamp and scope of affected traffic
page_texts.17:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#53-fail-closed-requirement]

### 5.3 Fail-Closed Requirement

The fail-closed requirement is a **domain-level architectural invariant**, not a configuration preference. It applies to every CBP instantiation in every traffic domain without exception.

**Definition:** When a domain control boundary's Decision Engine is unavailable, overloaded, or cannot reach a deterministic outcome within an architectural time bound, the Enforcement Point **must deny all affected flows**. No flow may transit a domain boundary in the absence of a valid, current permit decision from the Decision Engine.

**Rationale:** A fail-open boundary — one that permits traffic when the decision system is unavailable — eliminates the security property the domain provides. All four traffic domains exist to enforce explicit policy at platform boundaries. A domain boundary that fails open is architecturally equivalent to no boundary existing at that point.

**Scope of application:** The fail-closed requirement applies to:

- Full Decision Engine unavailability (crash, loss of connectivity to policy store)
- Partial Decision Engine degradation that cannot produce outcomes for the affected flow class
- Timeout conditions where the Decision Engine has not responded within the defined architectural time bound
- Decision Engine states where the policy store is unreachable and no current-session context exists that would support the specific decision required

**Scope exclusions:** The fail-closed requirement does **not** apply to:

- Flows for which a current, in-session permit already exists and the session has not expired — session continuity is a separate concern governed by session architecture standards
- Platform management and recovery traffic that is explicitly registered as an exception class through the platform exception management process
page_texts.18:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#54-policy-assertion-model]

### 5.4 Policy Assertion Model

A **Policy Assertion** is the structured representation of a permit decision emitted by a domain's Decision Engine and passed through the Enforcement Point to the downstream workload or domain. The Policy Assertion Model defines what a valid assertion must contain at a minimum — not its format, encoding, or protocol.

A valid Policy Assertion must carry the following capabilities, regardless of the format, encoding, or token standard used to realize it. The specific element schema, naming conventions, and encoding are defined in the downstream platform assertion standard.

| Capability | Architectural Purpose |
|------------|----------------------|
| **Verifiable issuer identity** | Enables downstream components to verify the assertion originates from an authorized boundary, not from a workload self-asserting its own authorization |
| **Authenticated subject identity** | The basis for least-privilege enforcement; downstream resources use this to scope access to the verified initiator |
| **Scoped authorization** | Prevents assertion reuse across unintended resources; limits blast radius of a compromised assertion |
| **Bounded validity period** | Prevents replay of stale assertions; constrains the implicit trust extension to the minimum necessary window |
| **Domain origin indicator** | Enables downstream domains to verify that traffic has traversed the expected domain control sequence |
| **Audit correlation link** | Enables end-to-end audit trail reconstruction across domain boundaries without requiring correlation by content |

**What a Policy Assertion is not:**

- A Policy Assertion is **not equivalent to a long-lived session token** — session continuity mechanisms are implementation concerns; the assertion model is a per-decision structural requirement
- A Policy Assertion is **not a network-layer artifact** — IP headers, security group tags, or routing labels do not constitute a Policy Assertion and do not satisfy this model
- A Policy Assertion is **not optional for cross-domain handoffs** — any traffic traversing a domain boundary without a valid Policy Assertion is non-conformant, regardless of network-layer policy

---

[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#6-traffic-control-domain-specifications]

## 6. Traffic Control Domain Specifications

Each domain specification defines how the CBP is instantiated for that domain — the specific entry conditions, the control authority model, the exit conditions, and the domain-specific constraints. Each domain's high-level required properties are defined in the parent ABB; this section specifies the **architectural composition** of each domain's control boundary.

---
page_texts.20:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#61-domain-1-external-in-ingress]

### 6.1 Domain 1: External-In (Ingress)

**Definition (from parent ABB):** Traffic originating outside the Platform Gainwell organizational trust boundary, destined for a hosted workload or service.
page_texts.21:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#cbp-instantiation]

#### CBP Instantiation

| CBP Component | External-In Instantiation |
|---------------|--------------------------|
| **Decision Engine** | Performs authentication of the external initiator and authorization of the requested resource; identity claims from the external party are verified against the platform's authoritative identity fabric before any authorization evaluation |
| **Enforcement Point** | Positioned at the platform's organizational ingress edge; all external traffic terminates at this point before any inward routing occurs; backend workloads are not directly reachable from external origins |
| **Audit Emitter** | Records every ingress access decision including authenticated subject identity, target resource, authorization outcome, and source context; PHI/PII-bearing paths require audit records sufficient to meet HIPAA audit control requirements |
| **Exception Handler** | When Decision Engine is unavailable, all ingress flows are denied; no external traffic transits to any backend workload in a fail-open state |
page_texts.22:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#entry-conditions]

#### Entry Conditions

Traffic enters Domain 1 when it originates from an origin outside the Platform Gainwell organizational trust boundary and is addressed to any Platform Gainwell workload or service endpoint. Entry is **the initiation of a connection** — it does not require the originator to have presented any credentials yet. Credential presentation and verification occur within the Decision Engine inside the domain boundary.
page_texts.23:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#control-authority-model]

#### Control Authority Model

The application layer is **solely authoritative** for External-In access decisions. Network-layer constructs — routing rules, security group permits, IP allowlisting — establish the connectivity prerequisite but do not constitute access authorization. A flow that has satisfied all network-layer prerequisites and has not yet traversed the application-layer Decision Engine is **not yet authorized**.
page_texts.24:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#exit-conditions]

#### Exit Conditions

Traffic exits Domain 1 when the Decision Engine has produced a permit outcome and the Enforcement Point has forwarded the request with a valid Policy Assertion to the target workload. The Policy Assertion represents the boundary of Domain 1 authority — from this point, the request is an **authenticated, authorized inbound request**, not an external request.
page_texts.25:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#domain-specific-constraints]

#### Domain-Specific Constraints

- **DEC-EI-01:** No External-In flow reaches a backend workload without traversing the application-layer Decision Engine. Network-only paths that reach a workload without application-layer enforcement are architecturally non-conformant.
- **DEC-EI-02:** The Enforcement Point for the External-In domain may aggregate multiple ingress control functions (request inspection, DDoS mitigation, rate limiting) but these do not substitute for the application-layer authentication and authorization that the Decision Engine must perform.
- **DEC-EI-03:** An external request that fails authentication produces an audit record and a deny outcome; the failure reason is not disclosed to the requestor in a form that enables enumeration of valid identities or resources.

---
page_texts.26:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#62-domain-2-internal-out-egress]

### 6.2 Domain 2: Internal-Out (Egress)

**Definition (from parent ABB):** Traffic originating from a Platform Gainwell workload or service, destined for an endpoint outside the organizational trust boundary.
page_texts.27:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#cbp-instantiation]

#### CBP Instantiation

| CBP Component | Internal-Out Instantiation |
|---------------|--------------------------|
| **Decision Engine** | Evaluates the workload's registered egress policy to determine whether the requested destination and traffic class are authorized; workload identity — not IP address — is the authorization subject |
| **Enforcement Point** | Positioned at the platform's organizational egress edge; all outbound traffic from workloads must route through this point before exiting; workloads cannot establish direct external connectivity that bypasses the egress boundary |
| **Audit Emitter** | Records every egress event including source workload identity, destination, protocol/port class, data volume context, and permit/deny outcome; egress audit trails are the primary mechanism for detecting data exfiltration |
| **Exception Handler** | When Decision Engine is unavailable, all egress flows are denied; no workload receives a fail-open egress path; workloads must be designed to tolerate egress unavailability without entering an error state that itself creates a security risk |
page_texts.28:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#entry-conditions]

#### Entry Conditions

Traffic enters Domain 2 when a Platform Gainwell workload or service initiates a connection to an endpoint outside the organizational trust boundary. Entry is triggered by the workload's outbound connection attempt — the workload's identity is established at the point of entry through the workload identity fabric required by the platform.
page_texts.29:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#control-authority-model]

#### Control Authority Model

Egress authorization is governed by a **registered egress policy** — a named, scoped policy artifact that authorizes a specific workload identity to communicate with a specific external destination class. Egress policy is not inferred from workload behavior or traffic patterns; it is explicitly declared and registered before the workload is admitted to production. An egress flow with no matching registered policy is denied.
page_texts.30:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#exit-conditions]

#### Exit Conditions

Traffic exits Domain 2 when the Enforcement Point has verified the registered egress policy, produced a permit outcome, and forwarded the outbound flow with associated Policy Assertion metadata toward the external destination. From this point, traffic is **governed outbound communication**, not unconstrained external traffic.
page_texts.31:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#domain-specific-constraints]

#### Domain-Specific Constraints

- **DEC-EO-01:** No workload may establish direct external connectivity outside the egress boundary. Network routing that reaches external destinations without traversing the Enforcement Point is architecturally non-conformant.
- **DEC-EO-02:** Egress policy registration is a platform onboarding gate — workloads without registered egress policy may not be admitted to production if they have declared external connectivity dependencies.
- **DEC-EO-03:** The Enforcement Point must be capable of distinguishing egress by workload identity, not only by IP address; multi-workload deployments on shared compute require workload-level differentiation in the egress audit trail.

---
page_texts.32:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#63-domain-3-east-west-inter-vpc--inter-account]

### 6.3 Domain 3: East-West (Inter-VPC / Inter-Account)

**Definition (from parent ABB):** Traffic between workloads, services, or accounts wholly within the Platform Gainwell organizational trust boundary but crossing a VPC or AWS account boundary.
page_texts.33:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#cbp-instantiation]

#### CBP Instantiation

| CBP Component | East-West Instantiation |
|---------------|------------------------|
| **Decision Engine** | Evaluates service-identity–based policy for the specific cross-boundary service call; policy is scoped to the requesting service identity and the target service identity, not to VPC or account membership |
| **Enforcement Point** | Centralized routing and inspection infrastructure positioned at the VPC/account boundary; no direct VPC-to-VPC or account-to-account path exists outside this enforcement point; all East-West flows are mediated |
| **Audit Emitter** | Records every cross-boundary authorization event including source service identity, source account/VPC, target service identity, target account/VPC, and permit/deny outcome; sufficient context to detect lateral movement is required |
| **Exception Handler** | When Decision Engine is unavailable, all East-West flows are denied; cross-boundary service calls must be designed with the expectation that the East-West boundary may be unavailable, and must fail gracefully rather than attempting alternative routing that bypasses the boundary |
page_texts.34:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#entry-conditions]

#### Entry Conditions

Traffic enters Domain 3 when a service or workload in one VPC or AWS account initiates a connection to a service or workload in a different VPC or AWS account, both within the Platform Gainwell organizational trust boundary. Entry is triggered by the cross-boundary connection attempt at the routing layer.
page_texts.35:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#control-authority-model]

#### Control Authority Model

East-West authorization is governed by **service identity policy** — a named, scoped policy that authorizes a specific source service identity to reach a specific target service identity across a specific boundary class. VPC membership, AWS account membership, or organizational unit affiliation do **not** constitute authorization. Two services in the same AWS Organization may be entirely unauthorized to communicate, depending on registered policy.
page_texts.36:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#exit-conditions]

#### Exit Conditions

Traffic exits Domain 3 when the Enforcement Point has verified the applicable service identity policy, produced a permit outcome, and forwarded the request toward the target service with a valid Policy Assertion. From this point, the request is an **authorized inter-service call** within the platform's internal trust boundary and may enter Domain 4 (Intra-VPC) at the target.
page_texts.37:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#domain-specific-constraints]

#### Domain-Specific Constraints

- **DEC-EW-01:** No direct VPC peering or account-to-account routing bypasses the centralized Enforcement Point. Any routing path that reaches a cross-boundary target without traversing the Enforcement Point is architecturally non-conformant.
- **DEC-EW-02:** Traffic that exits Domain 1 (External-In) and is destined for a workload in Account B must route through Domain 3 (East-West) on its cross-account leg — it does not remain in Domain 1 authority for inter-account routing.
- **DEC-EW-03:** Service identity used for East-West authorization must be issued by the platform's authoritative workload identity fabric; self-asserted or IP-derived identity does not satisfy the East-West authorization requirement.

page_texts.38:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#64-domain-4-intra-vpc-workload-to-workload]

### 6.4 Domain 4: Intra-VPC (Workload-to-Workload)

**Definition (from parent ABB):** Traffic between workloads co-located within the same VPC that have been admitted through applicable Policy Enforcement Points for their respective domain entries.
page_texts.39:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#cbp-instantiation]

#### CBP Instantiation

| CBP Component | Intra-VPC Instantiation |
|---------------|------------------------|
| **Decision Engine** | Evaluates workload-level segmentation policy for communication between co-located workloads; policy is based on workload identity and declared service dependencies, not IP address or VPC subnet |
| **Enforcement Point** | Enforced through network segmentation controls at the workload level; a workload cannot initiate communication to another co-located workload on ports or protocols not authorized by its segmentation policy, regardless of network adjacency |
| **Audit Emitter** | Records policy-significant Intra-VPC events proportional to the sensitivity classification of the data involved; all-traffic audit is not required at this domain but security-relevant events must be observable; the sensitivity threshold for what constitutes a security-relevant event is defined in downstream standards |
| **Exception Handler** | When segmentation enforcement is unavailable, deny-by-default posture applies; workloads may not fall back to unrestricted intra-VPC communication when enforcement is degraded |
page_texts.40:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#entry-conditions]

#### Entry Conditions

Traffic enters Domain 4 when a workload within a VPC initiates a connection to another workload within the same VPC, where both workloads have been admitted through their applicable domain entry controls. Domain 4 is **not the first domain entered by any external or cross-boundary traffic** — it is the innermost domain, reached only after applicable outer domain boundaries have been traversed.
page_texts.41:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#control-authority-model]

#### Control Authority Model

Intra-VPC authorization is governed by **workload segmentation policy** — a configured, dependency-declared policy that specifies which workload identities may communicate with which other workload identities, on which protocols and ports. Shared VPC membership is not a grant of communication rights. VPC co-location is a necessary routing condition, not an authorization condition.

Where the sensitivity of the data involved warrants it, workload identity — not IP address — is the authorization subject. For workloads processing PHI or PII, the workload identity basis is required; for low-sensitivity intra-VPC communication, IP-layer segmentation controls may suffice as determined by downstream standards.
page_texts.42:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#exit-conditions]

#### Exit Conditions

Intra-VPC is the **innermost domain**. Traffic does not "exit" Intra-VPC to another domain except when it initiates an outbound or cross-boundary request — at which point it enters Domain 2 (Internal-Out) or Domain 3 (East-West) at the appropriate boundary.
page_texts.43:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#domain-specific-constraints]

#### Domain-Specific Constraints

- **DEC-IV-01:** Co-location in the same VPC does not grant unrestricted lateral communication. Segmentation policy is required between workload groups regardless of their physical proximity.
- **DEC-IV-02:** Workloads from different application teams, different sensitivity classifications, or different logical domains co-located in the same VPC for operational reasons must satisfy authorization requirements equivalent to East-West domain traffic for their inter-team communication paths.
- **DEC-IV-03:** A workload that has passed through the External-In domain and been admitted to the platform does not carry that Domain 1 authorization into Intra-VPC — Intra-VPC authorization is evaluated independently based on the workload's segmentation policy.

[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#7-domain-handoff-model]

## 7. Domain Handoff Model

When traffic transitions from one domain to another, the receiving domain's Decision Engine must have sufficient context to make an independent authorization decision. The Domain Handoff Model defines the architectural contract for what must be present at a handoff point.
page_texts.45:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#71-handoff-principle]

### 7.1 Handoff Principle

Each domain is **architecturally sovereign** in its own authorization decision. No domain inherits authorization from a domain the traffic has already traversed. The fact that a flow was permitted by Domain 1 (External-In) does not authorize it within Domain 3 (East-West) or Domain 4 (Intra-VPC).
page_texts.46:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#72-handoff-contract]

### 7.2 Handoff Contract

At every point where traffic transitions between domains, the following must be present:

| Element | Requirement |
|---------|-------------|
| **Policy Assertion from the outgoing domain** | A valid Policy Assertion (per §5.4) from the domain the traffic is leaving, carrying the authorization context established in that domain |
| **Identity propagation** | The subject identity established in the outgoing domain must be propagated in a verifiable form to the receiving domain's Decision Engine; re-assertion of identity based on network position alone is not acceptable |
| **Audit correlation** | The handoff event itself must be recorded with the audit correlation identifiers from both the outgoing domain's permit record and the receiving domain's entry record, enabling cross-domain trace reconstruction |
| **Scope boundary enforcement** | The Policy Assertion from the outgoing domain may not be interpreted as extending to resources within the receiving domain unless the receiving domain explicitly recognizes and validates that extension |
page_texts.47:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#73-common-handoff-paths]

### 7.3 Common Handoff Paths

The following handoff paths occur in normal Platform Gainwell operation:

| Handoff | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **External-In → Intra-VPC** | Externally originated traffic, permitted by Domain 1, enters Domain 4 at the target workload within the same account; Domain 4 enforces segmentation policy independently |
| **External-In → East-West → Intra-VPC** | Externally originated traffic, permitted by Domain 1, is destined for a workload in a different account; it traverses Domain 3 on the cross-account leg before entering Domain 4 at the target |
| **Intra-VPC → East-West** | A workload in Domain 4 initiates a call to a workload in another account; the cross-boundary leg enters Domain 3 at the routing boundary |
| **Intra-VPC → Internal-Out** | A workload in Domain 4 initiates an outbound call to an external destination; the egress leg enters Domain 2 at the egress boundary |
| **East-West → Intra-VPC** | Traffic permitted to cross a VPC or account boundary by Domain 3 enters Domain 4 at the target workload |

[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#8-cross-domain-observability-requirements]

## 8. Cross-Domain Observability Requirements

The Security Operations architecture (`GUID-SEC-SECOPS-GEN-ARCH-REF-1.1.01`) provides the collection infrastructure; this section specifies the **minimum observable signals** that each domain boundary must make available, regardless of what collection mechanism realizes it.

These requirements define **what must be observable**, not how observations are stored, correlated, or alerted on — those are operational concerns addressed in downstream standards and the SecOps architecture.
page_texts.49:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#81-minimum-observable-signals-per-domain]

### 8.1 Minimum Observable Signals per Domain

| Signal Class | Ext-In | Int-Out | East-West | Intra-VPC |
|--------------|:------:|:-------:|:---------:|:---------:|
| **Authenticated subject identity** | Required | Required | Required | Required for PHI/PII workloads |
| **Target resource or service** | Required | Required | Required | Required for PHI/PII workloads |
| **Authorization outcome (permit/deny)** | Required | Required | Required | Required |
| **Policy evaluated** | Required | Required | Required | Required |
| **Timestamp of decision** | Required | Required | Required | Required |
| **Audit correlation identifier** | Required | Required | Required | Required |
| **Failure / exception events** | Required | Required | Required | Required |
| **Data volume context** | Recommended | Required | Recommended | Recommended for PHI/PII workloads |
| **Domain handoff events** | Required | Required | Required | Required |
page_texts.50:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#82-signal-availability-requirements]

### 8.2 Signal Availability Requirements

| Requirement | Description |
|-------------|-------------|
| **REQ-OBS-01** | Domain boundary signals must be available to the security operations telemetry collection infrastructure in a manner that supports the operational detection requirements defined in downstream SecOps standards; a domain boundary that produces only periodic batch audit output does not satisfy this requirement |
| **REQ-OBS-02** | Domain boundary signal streams must be observable even when the Decision Engine is in Exception Handler state; exception events are as important as normal permit/deny records |
| **REQ-OBS-03** | Domain boundary signals must be emitted to a path that is architecturally separate from the traffic being governed; a workload must not be able to suppress its own domain boundary audit signals |
| **REQ-OBS-04** | The audit correlation identifier must be consistent across the outgoing and receiving domain records for any given handoff, enabling end-to-end request tracing across domain boundaries |
| **REQ-OBS-05** | Gaps in domain boundary signal streams must themselves be observable — the telemetry collection infrastructure must be able to detect and alert on periods where expected signals are absent |

[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#9-architecture-decisions-embodied]

## 9. Architecture Decisions Embodied

This ABB directly extends the five architectural invariants from ADR-SEC-PG-001 with behavioral specifications:

| ADR-SEC-PG-001 Invariant | Extension in This ABB |
|--------------------------|----------------------|
| **No traditional DMZ** | §6.1 establishes that External-In's Enforcement Point at the edge eliminates the DMZ's semi-trusted zone function; the application layer is authoritative, not a network intermediary |
| **Application-layer primacy for ingress** | §6.1 (DEC-EI-01, Control Authority Model) establishes the architectural basis: network-layer permits are connectivity prerequisites, not access authorizations |
| **All traffic classified into four domains** | §6 (all domain specifications) + §7 (Domain Handoff Model) ensures that traffic in transit between domains is consistently classified and governed, not left in an ambiguous inter-domain state |
| **Implicit trust prohibited at all boundaries** | §5.4 (Policy Assertion Model) and §7.2 (Handoff Contract — identity propagation) ensure authorization is explicit and domain-sovereign; §7.1 (Handoff Principle) explicitly prohibits inherited authorization |
| **Cross-domain traffic requires explicit policy artifact** | §5.2 (Decision Engine) and §6 per-domain Control Authority Models all require a named, registered policy artifact; network state alone is not a policy artifact |

[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#10-architectural-qualification-criteria]

## 10. Architectural Qualification Criteria

The following criteria describe the properties that characterize a valid instantiation of the Control Boundary Pattern. They define the architectural boundary of this ABB — what the CBP *is* — not what implementations must operationally do. A realization that does not exhibit these properties addresses a different architectural intent and is not a CBP instantiation. Security standards that reference this ABB will translate these structural properties into operational requirements and conformance tests appropriate to their scope.

> **Structural properties incorporated elsewhere:** Per-flow authorization is a definitional property of the Decision Engine component (§5.2). Audit output path separation is a definitional property of the Audit Emitter component (§5.2). SBB realization guidance has been incorporated into §14.

| ID | Criterion |
|----|----------|
| CON-TC-01 | A conformant domain boundary exhibits all four CBP structural components: Decision Engine, Enforcement Point, Audit Emitter, and Exception Handler. A boundary lacking any component realizes a different pattern and does not constitute a CBP instantiation. |
| CON-TC-02 | Fail-closed behavior is a defining structural property of the Exception Handler component. A boundary that fails open does not exhibit the Exception Handler as specified in §5.2 and does not qualify as a CBP instantiation regardless of other controls present. |
| CON-TC-03 | Policy Assertions are domain-scoped. They carry no inherent authority in receiving domains; each receiving domain's Decision Engine makes an independent authorization determination. Domain authority does not propagate through assertion chain alone. |
| CON-TC-04 | Network-layer constructs — IP addresses, security group tags, subnet membership — describe routing conditions, not authorization. They do not constitute a Policy Assertion and do not satisfy the Handoff Contract defined in §7.2. |
| CON-TC-05 | Intra-VPC authorization is domain-sovereign. A workload's passage through an outer domain boundary does not extend its authorization within the Intra-VPC domain. Co-location of workloads from different teams, sensitivity classifications, or logical domains in the same VPC does not lower their inter-team authorization requirements below East-West equivalence. |

---

[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-PG-CLOUD-NETWORK-TRAFFIC-CONTROL-ABB-v1.md#11-assumptions]

## 11. Assumptions

| ID | Assumption | Implication If False |
|----|------------|----------------------|
| ASM-TC-01 | The platform's authoritative workload identity fabric (per GUID-SEC-IAM-REF-2.2.01) issues verifiable identity assertions to workloads at deployment | Without workload identity, East-West and Intra-VPC domain Decision Engines cannot perform identity-based authorization; IP-layer controls become the only available mechanism, which is explicitly insufficient for PHI/PII-bearing workloads |
| ASM-TC-02 | Workloads are onboarded through a platform process that registers their traffic profiles (declared ingress contract, egress destinations, inter-service dependencies) before production admission | Without pre-registration, the Decision Engine has no policy to evaluate against; unregistered workloads cannot be governed by any domain |
| ASM-TC-03 | The Security Operations architecture provides a telemetry collection path for domain boundary signals that is architecturally separate from the data plane workloads | Without a separate collection path, REQ-OBS-03 (signal suppression resistance) cannot be satisfied |
| ASM-TC-04 | The platform exception management process provides a documented, risk-accepted pathway for workloads that cannot immediately comply with all domain constraints | Without an exception pathway, legacy or transitional workloads create unregistered non-conformance that is invisible to governance |
| ASM-TC-05 | Cross-domain handoff paths (§7.3) are the authoritative enumeration of normal traffic flows; new handoff patterns that are not listed require explicit architectural review before being realized in any SBB | New handoff patterns create domain interaction conditions that this ABB has not specified; unreviewed patterns may violate the domain sovereignty principle in §7.1 |

| **NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 — AC-4** | Information Flow Enforcement | Domain-specific Control Authority Models in §6 define how information flow is controlled within and across each domain; the Design Engine evaluates information flow policy before any cross-domain transit |
| **NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 — AU-2 / AU-9 / AU-12** | Audit Events / Audit Protection / Audit Generation | Audit Emitter (CBP Component 3) and §8 Observability Requirements directly address these controls; REQ-OBS-03 (signal suppression resistance) addresses AU-9 (protection of audit information) |
| **NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 — SC-8** | Transmission Confidentiality and Integrity | CBP Enforcement Point and cross-domain encryption requirements address this control across all four domains |
| **NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 — SI-3 / SI-4** | Malicious Code Protection / System Monitoring | The Enforcement Point in Domain 1 (External-In) is the architectural location for application-layer inspection control; §8 observability requirements address SI-4's continuous monitoring requirement |
| **NIST SP 800-207 §2.1–2.3** | Zero Trust Architecture — per-request verification, no implicit trust, assume breach | CBP's Decision Engine is a per-request or per-flow construct (§5.2); §5.4 (Policy Assertion Model) formalizes the explicit verification artifact; fail-closed (§5.3) operationalizes the assume-breach posture |
| **ARC-AMPE v1.02** | CMS Transmission Security and Access Control for PHI (successor to MARS-E 2.0) | External-In domain constraints DEC-EI-01 through DEC-EI-03, combined with the Policy Assertion Model and Audit Emitter requirements, address ARC-AMPE access control and audit obligations for ACA, Medicaid, and Partner Entity data |

## 16. Success Criteria

A realization of this ABB is conformant when the following conditions hold in the produced environment:

| ID | Criterion |
|----|-----------|
| SC-TC-01 | **CBP completeness:** Every active traffic domain boundary in Platform Gainwell exhibits all four CBP structural components (Decision Engine, Enforcement Point, Audit Emitter, Exception Handler); any boundary missing a component is identified and tracked as a non-conformance |
| SC-TC-02 | **Fail-closed verification:** Domain boundary failure scenarios (Decision Engine unavailability, timeout, policy store loss) all result in deny outcomes; no fail-open path can be demonstrated through testing or analysis |
| SC-TC-03 | **Policy Assertion traceability:** For any given permitted inter-domain traffic flow, a valid Policy Assertion can be reconstructed from audit records, containing all six required elements in §5.4 |
| SC-TC-04 | **Domain sovereignty:** Passing through Domain 1 (External-In) does not automatically authorize a flow within Domain 3 (East-West) or Domain 4 (Intra-VPC); each domain's Decision Engine makes an independent authorization evaluation |
| SC-TC-05 | **Handoff auditability:** For any cross-domain handoff event (per §7.3), a correlated audit record exists in both the outgoing and receiving domain's audit stream, linked by the audit correlation identifier |
| SC-TC-06 | **Observability completeness:** All Required signal classes in §8.1 are demonstrably available to the security operations telemetry collection infrastructure for all four domains |
| SC-TC-07 | **Egress registration coverage:** All active egress flows from Platform Gainwell workloads to external destinations have a corresponding registered egress policy; no unregistered egress flows are present in the audit trail |
| SC-TC-08 | **Intra-VPC segmentation integrity:** No workload can demonstrate unrestricted lateral communication to co-located workloads that are not in its declared dependency set; access attempts to undeclared peers result in deny outcomes with audit records |
